claims.text: Choose snapshot and ongoing-change behavior explicitly. Debezium documents initial snapshots followed by streaming and separately configurable snapshot modes; the Spark source documents latest or timestamp startup when no offset exists. These are different bootstrap contracts, so switching tools requires a backfill-and-handoff design. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Full-document output is not sufficient evidence of faithful CDC replication. The Spark source filters events without fullDocument when change.stream.publish.full.document.only is enabled; Debezium separately models delete and tombstone events. Compare delete propagation before selecting either data path. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Use the MongoDB Spark Connector when a job needs to read MongoDB documents into Spark transformations and write results back; both MongoDB's guide and Databricks' MongoDB examples expose direct DataFrame reads and writes. (high confidence)

Meroxa's April 4, 2025 benchmark compares Conduit v0.13.2 with the MongoDB connector v0.2.2 against Kafka Connect v7.8.1 with MongoDB's Kafka connector v1.15.0. The tests use MongoDB-to-Kafka snapshot and CDC workloads on a four-vCPU t2.xlarge EC2 host, with Kafka and MongoDB provided via Docker containers. Meroxa reports about a 52% higher Conduit message rate in CDC; it does not benchmark the MongoDB Spark Connector, so the headline cannot rank that connector. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-04-04)
Kafka is optional for MongoDB-to-Spark streaming: MongoDB documents direct Spark micro-batches as well as a separate MongoDB Kafka source-to-Databricks pipeline. (high confidence)

Debezium offers an alternative capture boundary: its MongoDB connector records database changes in Kafka topics, and Lydtech's runnable demonstration separates database application writes from Kafka Connect capture. (high confidence)

MongoDB describes object-storage alternatives: Atlas Data Federation can export a one-time load to S3; a Kafka source plus S3 sink can stage ongoing changes for Databricks Auto Loader. Staging files still requires ingestion into Delta Lake. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-02)

Databricks distinguishes Spark Data Source API jobs for custom ETL and external writes, federation for governed ad-hoc querying, and managed ingestion for persistent replication. This generic comparison does not establish MongoDB support for every alternative; verify a source-specific support matrix before treating them as substitutes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-28)

Kafka buffering helps only after changes reach Kafka. Debezium warns that a long capture outage can exhaust MongoDB oplog history and that consumers must handle duplicate events under failures; adding Kafka does not remove source-retention and replay requirements. (low confidence)
